headline: Computational models infer gene regulation and interactions from existing omics data
label: Single Cell Predictive Modeling
summary: Dense single-cell, multi-omic, and genetic datasets now support predictive inference of causal, regulatory, and higher-order interaction structure.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference of molecular relationships from existing high-dimensional measurements rather than direct assay. CASE applies a Bayesian framework to jointly fine-map single-cell eQTLs across cell types, outperforming SuSiE and mvSuSiE in simulations and OneK1K data, with cell-type similarity as an explicit modeling feature. Dango, a self-attention hypergraph neural network, predicts higher-order trigenic interactions among yeast genes at scale. bioGraph infers proteo-transcriptomic networks through biologically informed heterogeneous graph learning, and lagCI infers time-lagged causal associations from dense multi-omic time series. A simulation study links regulatory network topology to cis- and trans-heritability of expression, and a multivariate genetic model resolves musculoskeletal disorders into three factors. What is new is the explicit modeling of cell-type specificity and similarity in single-cell eQTL fine-mapping. The remaining items are methodologically heterogeneous, and their connection is predictive modeling rather than a shared mechanism.
